transcript:
Meeting header
Date: 2027-09-14 15:00 PDT
Duration: 58 minutes
Location: Zoom
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Priya Nair (Redwood SE), Diego Alvarez (Redwood CSM); Evan Park (CTO), Priyanka Rao (Platform Eng), Liam O'Connor (AI Ops), Samir Patel (Security)

Auto-summary (auto-gen, may be incomplete):
- Kickoff for a 3-week runbook sprint to integrate Redwood Inference into Galene's production pipelines.
- Discussed network/VPC peering, security (KMS, audit logs), pilot capacity, success criteria (latency/throughput), and next steps.
- Agreed to share security pack and runbook template; schedule SE deep-dive and provision Dedicated trial.

Topics noted: network/VPC peering, SOC 2 / KMS / HSM, RBAC and SSO, quantization/profile recommendations, pilot acceptance criteria, runbook sprints, perf benchmarks (p50/p95/p99), rollback plans.

Action items (captured in CRM): see metadata.

Transcript:
[00:00] Maya: hey everyone, thanks for joining — uh we wanted to use this session to align on the runbook sprint and make sure the right people and stakeholders are in the loop. um I'll hand off to Priya for the technical framing and then Diego will go over the success criteria.
[00:22] Priya: thanks Maya. hi Evan, hi team. quick framing — from Redwood side the typical sprint we run is three weeks: week one is network and security, week two is pilot integration and smoke perf tests, week three is validation and ops handoff. that schedule is flexible but it helps customers get to a predictable pilot.
[00:40] Evan: that sounds good. our main constraint is we need to validate in our VPC, and we have strict KMS requirements — HSM-backed keys for any customer data. also legal wants audit logs retained for 2 years.
[00:55] Priya: copy that. Redwood Private supports customer-managed KMS and HSM integrations, and we can mirror audit logs to your logging pipeline. side note: sometimes the auto-transcript says KMS as "KMSes" — ignore that, but we will provide the security pack.
[01:10] Samir: when you say "mirror logs" is that direct kafka forwarding or S3 push? we have constrained egress policies for the cluster.
[01:18] Priya: generally we offer both — for Private deployments we can push compressed logs to your S3 bucket via an internal connector, or stream to your Kafka cluster if you open an IP range for us. we'll document the network flows in the runbook.
[01:30] Priya: quick question — are you planning to use Hosted API initially or go straight to Dedicated/private?
[01:36] Liam: we want to run within our VPC, so Private or Dedicated is the requirement. Hosted is a no-go for the pilot.
[01:43] Maya: ok good to know. that changes the provisioning path — we'll need network peering details and service account roles. Evan, can you confirm who on your networking team we should loop in?
[01:51] Evan: yeah that'll be Priyanka — she'll handle the peering request.
[01:55] Priyanka: yep, I'll collect the VPC CIDRs and put together the security checklist. and we do need SAML/SSO for RBAC integration — we manage identities via Azure AD.
[02:06] Diego: we support SAML SSO and SCIM for user provisioning; we can map Redwood roles to your RBAC groups. we'll surface that in the runbook.
[02:14] Samir: any experience with SOC 2 auditors asking about model output logs? they want to know what PII filtering we have.
[02:23] Priya: yes — we can redact or omit certain low-level tokens from logs; Redwood has configurable retention and PII redaction at the request path. we'll include the policy options in the security pack.
[02:35] Evan: great. on performance: we have latency SLOs for our internal chat assistant — p99 under 300ms for <1k token responses. cost is also a factor; we want to understand batching and quantization recommendations.
[02:48] Priya: for p99 sub-300 that's achievable depending on model and hardware choice. two levers: kernel selection / quantization and batching. Redwood's runtime supports continuous batching and KV cache which helps with chat workloads. for on-prem/dedicated we can recommend a quantization profile — e.g., 4-bit static profile — to hit cost targets with small latency tradeoffs.
[03:10] Liam: can you run benchmarks on our sequences? our typical session is 120–200 tokens.
[03:15] Priya: yeah we usually ask for 5–10 representative prompts for the benchmarking run. we'll schedule a perf slot where we run those against a Dedicated node.
[03:23] Maya: for timeline — we proposed a two-week pilot. Diego, can you outline acceptance criteria?
[03:28] Diego: sure. suggested pilot acceptance criteria: 1) integration completeness: VPC peering + SSO + log forwarding, 2) perf: median latency and p95/p99 within agreed thresholds (p99 < 300ms target), 3) quality: 50 sample prompts pass quality gate (customer-provided prompt set), 4) stability: no critical errors during a 48-hour soak at expected load. we can refine.
[03:48] Evan: that looks good, except we want p50 < 100ms if possible.
[03:52] Priya: we'll try to hit that right away but it depends on model choice — smaller distilled models will hit lower p50s.
[03:59] Samir: security-wise, two questions: is there support for bringing-your-own-HSM, and can we get per-request audit metadata?
[04:08] Priya: yes we have BYO-KMS/HSM integrations for Private installs. per-request audit metadata is available; we can push a structured audit stream to your SIEM.
[04:18] Priyanka: networking detail — our infra team blocks egress except approved endpoints. what IP ranges do you need for peering?
[04:25] Priya: for a Dedicated pilot within your cloud account we typically ask you to create a VPC and we deploy nodes there — so egress is under your control. if we do cross-account peering there's a small list of control-plane endpoints to allow; we'll include exact CIDRs in the runbook template.
[04:41] Evan: perfect. about rollback — if the model rollout degrades quality we need automatic fallback to a previous model and a canary window. does Redwood support that?
[04:50] Priya: yes, rollouts are first-class: you can canary, A/B, and have automatic fallback policies. we'll show the rollout example in the runbook.
[04:58] Maya: quick pause — I'm seeing a couple of hand raises in chat asking for a sample runbook. Priya will share that.
[05:05] Priya: i'll share the runbook template after the call — it has sections: contacts, network, IAM, model selection, perf benchmarks, acceptance criteria, rollback plan, incident runbooks.
[05:16] Liam: for benchmarks we also want token-level cost breakdowns by route — can that be exported?
[05:21] Diego: yes Redwood Console gives token-level cost/latency breakdowns per route and model; we can export a CSV for analysis.
[05:28] Evan: are there any compliance limitations with data residency? we have EMEA data nodes and need to ensure inference and logs reside in EU.
[05:36] Priya: for Private deployments you can choose region placement. for Hosted we have region restrictions; Dedicated we can pin nodes to your preferred region. we'll document residency options and how to configure them.
[05:48] Samir: one more on encryption — do tokens remain encrypted in KV cache? that was a question from our privacy team.
[05:55] Priya: yes sensitive KV cache entries can be encrypted at rest with customer keys. we'll map the key lifecycle in the runbook.
[06:03] Evan: ok great. shifting to logistics — can we outline the proposed sprint week-by-week?
[06:09] Priya: yeah quickly: Week 0 (pre-sprint): gather contacts, sample prompts, and access (VPC/SSO). Week 1: network, IAM, KMS setup, basic smoke test. Week 2: deploy pilot routes, run benchmarks, collect metrics. Week 3: validation, docs and ops handoff, finalize acceptance.
[06:28] Diego: and within that we'll schedule a 2-hour SE deep-dive in week 2 to run perf and iterate on quant profiles.
[06:35] Priyanka: the pre-sprint items — I'll send the CIDR and idp metadata by end of Friday.
[06:40] Evan: i'll check with legal re: retention and confirm if 2 years is ok; might need 18 months but we'll confirm.
[06:46] Maya: thanks. any concerns about costs during the pilot? we can cap spend on the Dedicated trial if needed.
[06:53] Liam: cap helps — also would like visibility into per-route cost to show product team.
[06:57] Diego: we'll enable per-route metrics in the Console and set budget alerts.
[07:03] Samir: can you also provide a sample SSO integration flow? our SAML provider has strict cert rotation.
[07:09] Priya: yes sample SAML flow and cert rotation steps are in the runbook. we'll highlight cert-rotation automation too.
[07:16] Speaker 1: (brief crosstalk) yeah that's helpful.
[07:20] Maya: ok nearing the end — let's recap next steps. Diego, do you want to summarize acceptance criteria and owners?
[07:25] Diego: sure — acceptance criteria recap: network + SSO + logs in place; perf targets: p50 < 100ms (where possible), p99 < 300ms target; quality gate on customer prompt set; 48-hour soak stability. Owners: Maya will send security docs; Priya will share runbook and config examples; Evan/Priyanka will provide VPC and IDP info; Diego to draft pilot metrics doc.
[07:47] Evan: sounds good.
[07:49] Maya: thanks everyone — we'll shoot the security pack and runbook over by Thursday, and schedule the SE deep-dive for next week.
[07:57] Priya: i'll put the runbook link in slack and invite the infra contacts.
[08:02] Samir: thanks all.
[08:04] Maya: meeting adjourned.

(Transcript notes: occasional transcription errors present; some product names may have been mis-transcribed like "Redwood Dedicate" or "KV cache" spelled differently. See attached security pack link in follow-up — not included in transcript.)
